The Police Sub-Inspector of R.T. Nagar Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

After marriage, CW1 resided at No.136, 11th Cross, CBI Road,
Lakshmaiah Block, Ganganagar, wherein the accused No.1 under influence of alcohol subjected CW1 to mental and physical cruelty and forcibly took her to his native place.

Further, in his native place accused No.1 to 4 were ill-treated CW1 for fetching additional dowry from her parental house,
therefore, her parents namely CW2 and CW3 arranged a separate house for accused No.1 and CW1 at No.97, 3 rd Main, Ganganagar, Binny Mill Road within the limits of R.T.Nagara Police Station,
Bengaluru.

Such being, on 17-12-2017 at 2 pm CW1 found the accused No.1 with unknown lady at above said house, when CW1 questioned about the said illicit relationship, the accused No.1 picked up quarrel with CW1, abused and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, thereby accused persons have committed alleged offences.
3. First Information Report:

On receipt of first information from CW1, CW12 namely Sri Thirthappa,
HC of R.T. Nagara Police Station registered Crime No.160/2019 against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D P Act, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.

4. Investigation: Thereafter CW13 Sri Mithun Shilpi, PI drawn spot mahazar on 07-08-2019,
recorded the statement of witnesses, secured the photographs and documents and submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

has been framed, read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 4 in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW1 namely Smt. ring to the accused.

4 for fetching more dowry.

In the month of October 2014, the accused had a quarrel with her, abused and beaten her, on 07-12-2014, when she came home from work, the door was locked and after half an hour, a woman opened the door, when she asked about her, accused picked up quarrel with her and hence she left the house and filed a complaint as per Ex.P1, the police conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P2.

Evidence of Prosecution must be established that the accused persons subjected the PW1 to mental and physical cruelty.

Mere omnibus statement regarding harassment does not ipso facto makes out a case under section 498A IPC, prosecution is required to prove the overt acts attributed by the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt and the said principle is appreciated in case of Sakharam and another vs State of Maharastra reported in (2003) 12 SCC 368.

Basing this decision,
the present cases are taken up for discussion.

17. It is relevant to reiterate Section 498A of Indian Penal Code which reads as under Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty -- Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

-- For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

For commission of an offence under Section 498- A of IPC, the following necessary ingredients require to be satisfied:
(a) The woman must be married;
(b) She must be subjected to cruelty or harassment; and (c) Such cruelty or harassment must have been shown either by husband of the woman or by the relative of her husband and the said principle is appreciated in the case of U. Suvetha v. State reported in (2009) 6 SCC 757.
18.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision in the case of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and another reported in (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."
